items.title: New AI method uses engineering knowledge to estimate disaster damage from incomplete satellite imagery
items.excerpt: A new technology has been developed that can rapidly predict city-scale structural damage even when portions of satellite imagery are obscured by clouds or smoke immediately after a disaster. The method folds engineering knowledge into the model so missing pixels do not break the estimate.

items.title: Spiking neural network learns to predict what will happen, when, and how likely it is
items.excerpt: Before an event arrives, the brain can predict what it will be, when it will occur and how likely it is. A new study proposes a single population of spiking neurons that learns all three together, in a way that is compatible with biological circuits.

items.title: Can scientists build a lie detector for AI chatbots?
items.excerpt: One of the biggest issues with AI chatbots today is that they can still share false information, according to Northeastern experts. Researchers are probing whether a model's internal states can be read to flag when it is not telling the truth.

items.title: Machine learning detects bacterial invasion and DNA damage in human cells
items.excerpt: Researchers built MALVINA, a machine learning method that reads microscopy images to measure how efficiently bacteria enter human cells and trigger DNA damage at single-cell resolution. The same bacterial count can hide very different infection patterns.

items.title: New algorithm makes maps of gene activity easier to compare while preserving cell-level detail
items.excerpt: Spatial transcriptomics can reveal where thousands of genes are active across a tissue at single-cell resolution. A new algorithm aligns two such maps that are rotated or stretched without smoothing away cell-level detail.

items.title: Unlocking AI as a research tool for plant microscopy
items.excerpt: Software from University of Queensland scientists could help AI platforms overcome a blind spot limiting their value in plant research. Even advanced vision-language models struggled to interpret plant microscopy images.

items.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs
items.source: GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News
items.excerpt: A hybrid digital twin that combines mechanistic modeling with artificial intelligence could enable autonomous biomanufacturing, letting a lab run and correct its own bioprocesses.

items.title: Adding Low-Fidelity Data to ML Training Sets Could Yield Better Process Models
items.source: GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News
items.excerpt: Combining low-fidelity trend information with empirical data to train models can improve their accuracy and reduce costs, researchers report — a counterintuitive result for labs short on clean data.

items.title: New Calibration Framework Improves Confidence in AI Virtual Cell Models
items.source: GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News
items.excerpt: Metrics such as mean squared error and control-referenced Pearson correlation are frequently miscalibrated when used to judge AI virtual cell models, according to the authors, who propose a calibration framework instead.

items.title: Haiqu Releases AgenticOS to Plan and Check Quantum Research
items.excerpt: Haiqu launched AgenticOS, a system that coordinates specialized AI agents to plan, validate and prepare quantum research experiments.

items.title: As AI Closed In on 'Unique Games' Proof, Researchers Raced to Beat the Machines
items.excerpt: In the shadow of a rumored AI proof of one of the biggest problems in their field, three computer scientists rushed to publish their own milestone result.

items.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
items.excerpt: Mathematicians are facing the sudden shift with grief, anger, and a desperate search for fresh ideas: 'If we don't adapt, there's just no more math in 50 years.'

items.title: Don't be fooled-LLMs don't reason
items.excerpt: Ten years after AlphaGo's match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today's AI still isn't tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

items.title: How AI helped bring an ancient tomb dating to before the Roman Empire back to life
items.excerpt: Pairing artificial intelligence with acoustic technology helped reveal an Etruscan tomb in new light, reconstructing faded wall paintings and the sound of the chamber.

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Attachment is the term psychologists use for the most significant relationships that hold people's lives together — and researchers are now applying it to how people bond with chatbots.

items.title: What is AI model distillation, and why is it so hard to stop?
items.excerpt: Anthropic and OpenAI accused Chinese AI developers of mining their models' answers to train cheaper copycats. Here's how distillation works and why it's so hard to stop.

items.title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
items.excerpt: The technique behind Bolmo, Ai2's fully open byte-level language models, is now published in Nature, with new checkpoints showing the approach generalizes beyond Olmo to other model families.

items.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
items.excerpt: Ai2 is releasing AstaBrief, an 8B open-weights model for generating cited scientific reports, available in Asta's Fast mode or to download and run on your own infrastructure.

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for protecting wildlife around the world, from autonomous drones counting animals to models that pick out calls in field audio.

items.title: SynthID Bio: Watermarking methods for synthetic biology
items.excerpt: DeepMind introduced SynthID Bio, a method that embeds invisible, detectable signatures into AI-designed biological sequences and protein structures. Watermarked proteins bound their targets as well as unmarked ones.

items.title: Limitations of Genomic Foundation Models for Decoding Regulatory Mechanisms in ALS
items.excerpt: Genomic foundation models promise to infer regulatory consequences of genetic variants directly from DNA sequence. This preprint evaluates AlphaGenome on ALS genetics without disease-specific fine-tuning and finds the predictions fall short of clinical utility.

items.title: RGI-Toolkit: Differentiable Restraints for Controllable Biomolecular Structure Prediction
items.excerpt: Diffusion models have advanced biomolecular structure prediction; restraint-guided inference corrects the denoiser at each step. RGI-Toolkit packages differentiable restraints so experimental data or a target conformation can steer the prediction.
